request: Reduce COPS push validation time and measure the effect of pytest worker counts on Ubuntu.
scope: Run root pytest once with coverage in the standard push profile. Compare serial pytest with two and four workers in the benchmark.
setup: Use the repository’s Python test environment and a dedicated Ubuntu amd64 benchmark runner.
constraints: Keep the existing coverage policy, draft routing, and all eleven hosted gates in force.

steps.action: Move coverage instrumentation into the root pytest invocation used by the standard push profile.

verify.expected: The full profile requests one coverage-bearing root run, ordinary make check keeps its existing command, and the draft still defers the full suite.

steps.action: Measure each worker count and give the two timestamp-dependent cases stable collection IDs.

verify.expected: The benchmark accepts equivalent outcomes and rejects incomplete reports. Both timestamp fixtures still reject invalid observations.

acceptance.entrypoint: make check with the push profile’s coverage option
acceptance.given: The standard push profile needs root pytest and coverage.
acceptance.when: Run the repository check with the coverage option.
acceptance.then: The root test suite runs once with the existing branch coverage policy.

acceptance.entrypoint: make check with the push profile’s coverage option
acceptance.given: Root pytest returns a failing status.
acceptance.then: The check fails and skips reporting partial coverage.

acceptance.given: The canonical push gate receives the draft profile.
acceptance.when: Compare the draft and standard commands.
acceptance.then: Only the full suite is deferred for the draft.

acceptance.given: Worker reports contain the same test IDs and outcomes in a different order.
acceptance.then: The comparison accepts the equivalent results.

acceptance.given: A benchmark report is incomplete or repeats a test.
acceptance.then: The benchmark rejects the invalid report.

acceptance.given: A fixture inventory carries an invalid or future measurement timestamp.
acceptance.then: Validation rejects the timestamp using stable pytest IDs.

acceptance.given: An inert fixture observation is false, stale, or mismatched.
acceptance.then: Verification fails closed and leaves the canary unverified.
